railway_timetable_recovery.title: The timetable after the war
railway_timetable_recovery.description: The tracks are usable again, but freight trains and returning families are competing for the same damaged junctions. Reopening a line is not the same as making it work.

options.title: Repair the junctions before expanding service
options.consequence: A costly repair programme clears a little of the physical damage and restores confidence.

options.title: Let local operators restore a limited service
options.consequence: Less public money buys a slower recovery; neglected settlements grow impatient.

options.title: Give freight the first available paths
options.consequence: Factories receive their inputs sooner, while passengers bear the inconvenience.

emergency_maintenance_reserve.title: An emergency maintenance reserve
emergency_maintenance_reserve.description: Rising prices have consumed the money set aside for routine repairs. Engineers want a protected reserve before deferred maintenance becomes a chain of failures.

options.title: Protect the maintenance budget
options.consequence: The treasury takes the hit now rather than leaving residents to pay later.

options.title: Pass the cost into service charges
options.consequence: The accounts recover, but households have less to live on.

options.title: Schedule only the most urgent repairs
options.consequence: Limited work buys time without restoring the reserve or cancelling its future bill.
